She knelt in the garden, fingers digging into the cool soil, the rich, dark earth crumbling beneath her touch. A light breeze played with the stray strands of hair that had escaped her braid, the tendrils brushing against her cheeks like whispers of forgotten memories. She could hear the distant sound of laughter from the street, a reminder of a world that was moving on without her, but in that moment, all she could focus on was the rhythm of her heartbeat, the pulse of life that echoed in the quiet.

“Are you going to sit there all day, or are you actually going to help me?” Lucas’s voice broke through her reverie, teasing yet warm, like the sun that peeked through the leaves overhead. His shadow stretched across her work, a momentary cloud that brought a chill to her skin, but she welcomed it, the contrast grounding her in the now.

“I’m contemplating the meaning of life,” she shot back, a playful smirk tugging at the corners of her mouth as she tossed a handful of dirt playfully in his direction. It landed harmlessly on his cheek, a soft smudge against his tanned skin. He wiped at it, feigning offense, but his eyes sparkled with amusement, the kind that made her heart flutter unexpectedly.

“Right. And I suppose you’ll find all the answers buried out here?” he said, leaning down, his face inches from hers, the warmth radiating off him a stark contrast to the coolness of the earth. She could see the flecks of gold in his brown eyes, the way they danced with mischief and something deeper, something that urged her to let her guard down, even just a little.
